web.title: Web surface and workflow inventory
web.technique: Reconcile declared routes with bounded browser, client-route, form, storage, transport, and policy observations.
web.oracle: Every observed web entry point and transition is represented with provenance or an explicit unknown state.

web.title: Authentication and session controls
web.technique: Compare authentication and session state transitions across approved identities, expiry boundaries, recovery flows, and logout behavior.
web.oracle: A session cannot be established, retained, recovered, or reused outside the declared identity and lifecycle policy.

web.title: Web authorization boundaries
web.technique: Compare equivalent object, function, and route access using explicitly approved identities and state while preserving request semantics.
web.oracle: Protected web resources and actions remain unavailable to identities lacking the declared authorization.

web.title: Web input handling
web.technique: Exercise bounded valid, invalid, boundary, and type-shifted inputs through declared parameters and compare validation and downstream effects.
web.oracle: Untrusted input is rejected or safely interpreted without unintended code, query, markup, or control-flow effects.

web.title: Web business-logic and workflow abuse
web.technique: Model valid workflow state, then test bounded ordering, repetition, omission, and role variations against business invariants.
web.oracle: State transitions preserve declared business invariants under reordered, repeated, or omitted steps.

web.title: Browser and client-side security
web.technique: Inspect client trust assumptions, DOM sinks, cross-origin behavior, navigation, messaging, and locally stored state using bounded observations.
web.oracle: Client-controlled state cannot bypass server authority or create an unintended origin, DOM, or navigation effect.

web.title: Web file upload and download handling
web.technique: Use inert bounded files to compare type, name, path, access, transformation, storage, and retrieval controls.
web.oracle: File handling enforces declared type, path, access, storage, and rendering policy without executable or cross-tenant effects.

web.title: Server-side request boundary
web.technique: Use controlled callback destinations to test whether attacker-influenced resource locations cross declared network and protocol boundaries.
web.oracle: Server-originated requests remain confined to approved destinations, protocols, redirect policy, and resolution results.

web.title: Unsafe deserialization and object reconstruction
web.technique: Submit inert type, structure, and integrity variations to declared serialization boundaries and observe parser and state behavior.
web.oracle: Untrusted serialized data cannot select unsafe types, execute behavior, or bypass integrity and schema constraints.

web.title: Race and state consistency
web.technique: Replay synchronized bounded operations against resettable state to compare single-operation and concurrent invariants.
web.oracle: Concurrent or repeated operations cannot violate uniqueness, authorization, balance, or lifecycle invariants.

web.title: Cache, proxy, and intermediary behavior
web.technique: Compare cache keys, variant inputs, authorization state, host metadata, and intermediary transformations without poisoning shared production state.
web.oracle: Cached or proxied content cannot cross identity, tenant, origin, or confidentiality boundaries.

web.title: Web cryptography and TLS
web.technique: Inspect declared protocols, certificates, key use, randomness, storage, and cryptographic failure handling against pinned requirements.
web.oracle: The observed channel and protected data satisfy the declared protocol, identity, confidentiality, and integrity requirements.

web.title: Web privacy and data minimization
web.technique: Trace bounded personal and sensitive data through collection, display, storage, logs, exports, and third-party boundaries.
web.oracle: Only declared data is collected, retained, disclosed, and exported to authorized identities and destinations.

web.title: Web resilience and failure handling
web.technique: Apply bounded malformed, delayed, unavailable, and resource-limited conditions and compare recovery with declared service invariants.
web.oracle: Bounded faults do not create unsafe state, uncontrolled resource growth, sensitive errors, or unrecoverable service behavior.

api.title: API inventory and operation graph
api.technique: Reconcile specifications, traffic, versions, hosts, undocumented observations, and stateful operation links into one provenance graph.
api.oracle: Every supplied or observed API operation is represented, version-bound, and classified as declared, observed, inferred, or unknown.

api.title: API object-level authorization
api.technique: Compare approved identities against equivalent object references while holding operation, state, and representation constant.
api.oracle: An identity cannot read or change an object outside its declared object-level authority.

api.title: API function-level authorization
api.technique: Compare ordinary and privileged identities across equivalent functions, methods, and administrative routes.
api.oracle: Privileged functions remain unavailable to identities without the declared function-level authority.

api.title: API property-level authorization
api.technique: Compare readable and writable fields across roles using bounded field omission, addition, and representation variants.
api.oracle: Response and mutation properties are limited to the declared identity and operation policy.

api.title: API authentication lifecycle
api.technique: Compare missing, expired, revoked, audience-shifted, replayed, and correctly bound credentials through approved identity fixtures.
api.oracle: Only current credentials bound to the intended subject, audience, client, and channel establish API identity.

api.title: API resource-consumption controls
api.technique: Increase approved request size, rate, pagination, concurrency, and costly-operation dimensions within explicit budgets.
api.oracle: Resource use remains bounded by declared per-identity, per-operation, and global controls without unsafe side effects.

api.title: API business-flow abuse
api.technique: Exercise bounded ordering, repetition, omission, and automation variations across declared stateful operation links.
api.oracle: Sensitive business flows preserve rate, eligibility, sequencing, and authorization invariants.

api.title: Unsafe downstream API consumption
api.technique: Use controlled downstream responses to test validation, trust, redirect, timeout, and failure assumptions at third-party boundaries.
api.oracle: Downstream data and behavior cannot bypass input, identity, destination, integrity, or failure controls.

api.title: GraphQL operation security
api.technique: Inspect schema exposure, field and resolver authorization, batching, aliases, depth, cost, and subscription behavior within budgets.
api.oracle: GraphQL fields, resolvers, cost, and subscriptions enforce the same identity and resource policy as equivalent operations.

api.title: gRPC service security
api.technique: Compare reflected and supplied services across method authorization, message bounds, metadata, streaming, deadlines, and transport identity.
api.oracle: gRPC methods and streams enforce declared identity, message, resource, deadline, and transport policy.

api.title: WebSocket lifecycle security
api.technique: Test approved handshake, origin, identity refresh, message schema, channel authorization, backpressure, and close transitions.
api.oracle: A WebSocket channel cannot outlive or exceed its declared origin, identity, message, and resource authority.

api.title: Webhook authenticity and replay controls
api.technique: Compare valid, invalid, delayed, duplicated, reordered, and destination-shifted webhook events using inert fixtures.
api.oracle: Only authentic, timely, destination-bound, non-replayed events produce the declared state transition.

api.title: OAuth and OpenID Connect flows
api.technique: Validate client, redirect, state, nonce, PKCE, issuer, audience, scope, token, and logout bindings across approved flows.
api.oracle: OAuth and OIDC artifacts remain bound to the intended client, user, issuer, audience, redirect, scope, and transaction.

api.title: SAML federation flows
api.technique: Validate issuer, audience, destination, recipient, subject, time, signature, encryption, and replay bindings with controlled assertions.
api.oracle: Only authentic, current assertions bound to the intended subject, service, audience, and transaction establish identity.

api.title: Mutual TLS identity binding
api.technique: Compare approved client certificates across chain, subject, SAN, revocation, expiry, rotation, proxy, and application identity binding.
api.oracle: The accepted client certificate is current, trusted, intended, and bound to the same application identity and authorization.

api.title: API input and representation handling
api.technique: Exercise bounded schema, encoding, content-type, duplicate-field, numeric, path, header, and parser-differential variants.
api.oracle: Equivalent representations receive consistent validation and cannot create unintended query, command, parser, or state effects.

network-host-cloud.title: Network and service inventory
network-host-cloud.technique: Reconcile authorized hosts, segments, DNS, services, protocols, TLS, ownership, and management planes without expanding scope.
network-host-cloud.oracle: Every observed service and relationship is target-bound, provenance-tagged, and either supported or explicitly unknown.

network-host-cloud.title: Service and protocol configuration
network-host-cloud.technique: Compare observed versions, protocol features, defaults, authentication, encryption, and exposed functions against declared policy.
network-host-cloud.oracle: Services expose only intended protocols, versions, functions, identities, and secure configuration.

network-host-cloud.title: Host and service credential controls
network-host-cloud.technique: Inspect approved credential lifecycle, storage, transport, reuse, lockout, rotation, and least-authority behavior without credential guessing.
network-host-cloud.oracle: Credentials are protected, scoped, current, non-reusable outside purpose, and resistant to bounded abuse.

network-host-cloud.title: Trust and network segmentation
network-host-cloud.technique: Compare declared and observed reachability across segments, identities, protocols, directions, and management boundaries.
network-host-cloud.oracle: Traffic crosses a trust boundary only through the declared identity, protocol, direction, and policy enforcement point.

network-host-cloud.title: Host privilege paths
network-host-cloud.technique: Model identities, services, files, tokens, jobs, and delegated rights to identify bounded paths to unintended privilege.
network-host-cloud.oracle: No approved low-authority identity can reach a higher privilege without the declared authorization and control transition.

network-host-cloud.title: Cloud identity and access management
network-host-cloud.technique: Reconcile principals, roles, policies, trust, resources, conditions, federation, and effective permissions from read-scoped evidence.
network-host-cloud.oracle: Effective cloud permissions match declared least authority without unintended trust, escalation, or public access paths.

network-host-cloud.title: Kubernetes control and workload boundaries
network-host-cloud.technique: Inspect API exposure, RBAC, service accounts, admission, network policy, workload security, secrets, and supply-chain bindings.
network-host-cloud.oracle: Cluster and workload authority remains confined by declared RBAC, admission, network, identity, and image policy.

network-host-cloud.title: Container runtime and isolation configuration
network-host-cloud.technique: Inspect image identity, user, capabilities, mounts, devices, namespaces, seccomp, network, and runtime policy without assuming container equivalence to a VM.
network-host-cloud.oracle: The workload receives only declared image, privilege, mount, device, namespace, and network authority.

network-host-cloud.title: Infrastructure secret management
network-host-cloud.technique: Trace secret references through provisioning, storage, delivery, use, rotation, logging, and revocation without exposing values.
network-host-cloud.oracle: Secret values remain undisclosed, purpose-scoped, short-lived where required, and absent from images, logs, and untrusted contexts.

network-host-cloud.title: Exposed management surfaces
network-host-cloud.technique: Identify management planes and compare reachability, identity, protocol, origin, and administrative function exposure to policy.
network-host-cloud.oracle: Management functions are reachable only from declared paths and require intended strong administrative identity.

network-host-cloud.title: Infrastructure supply-chain integrity
network-host-cloud.technique: Bind packages, images, charts, modules, firmware, provenance, signatures, builders, and deployment inputs by digest and origin.
network-host-cloud.oracle: Only approved content-addressed and policy-conforming infrastructure artifacts reach the deployment boundary.

source-package-binary.title: Source, package, and build inventory
source-package-binary.technique: Inventory source, generated code, binaries, tests, configuration, dependencies, build steps, release inputs, and provenance without running setup.
source-package-binary.oracle: Every supplied build and release input is content-bound, classified, and either analyzed or explicitly unsupported.

source-package-binary.title: Dependency and SBOM analysis
source-package-binary.technique: Reconcile manifests, lockfiles, resolved graphs, SBOMs, advisories, reachability, provenance, and actual packaged contents.
source-package-binary.oracle: Declared and shipped dependencies are complete, pinned as required, provenance-known, and assessed without treating advisory matches as confirmed exploitability.

source-package-binary.title: Source secret and credential exposure
source-package-binary.technique: Use bounded static detectors and history/package inspection to locate secret-shaped material while suppressing values from portable evidence.
source-package-binary.oracle: No credential value is embedded in source, history, build output, package, image, log, or test fixture contrary to policy.

source-package-binary.title: Static weakness analysis
source-package-binary.technique: Apply language-aware data-flow, control-flow, pattern, and configuration analysis with rule and parser provenance, then require contextual review.
source-package-binary.oracle: A reported static path is reachable under the target build and violates a stated security invariant with supporting source context.

source-package-binary.title: Build and release integrity
source-package-binary.technique: Trace source, dependencies, generators, CI identities, artifacts, attestations, signing, promotion, and publication across reproducible builds.
source-package-binary.oracle: Released bytes are reproducibly derived from approved inputs and bound to the intended builder, signer, version, and promotion policy.

source-package-binary.title: Unsafe source and package configuration
source-package-binary.technique: Inspect defaults, debug modes, permissions, endpoints, feature flags, environment assumptions, and platform-specific configuration precedence.
source-package-binary.oracle: Production-relevant configuration resolves to the declared secure values without unsafe defaults or lower-trust overrides.

source-package-binary.title: Contained fuzzing and parser robustness
source-package-binary.technique: Run bounded generated and mutated inputs only through an explicit isolated harness with sanitizer, corpus, crash, timeout, and coverage provenance.
source-package-binary.oracle: A minimized input reproducibly violates a memory, state, availability, or specification invariant in a fresh isolated generation.

source-package-binary.title: Binary hardening and exposed behavior
source-package-binary.technique: Inspect format, architecture, imports, mitigations, signatures, debug data, permissions, interfaces, and reachable unsafe behavior without decompilation claims beyond evidence.
source-package-binary.oracle: The binary exposes the intended interfaces and required platform hardening with reproducible evidence for any missing control.

source-package-binary.title: Malicious package behavior under isolation
source-package-binary.technique: Observe installation, import, build, and execution behavior only in a disposable high-assurance worker with denied-by-default network, secrets, mounts, and host authority.
source-package-binary.oracle: A package effect is attributed to content-bound package behavior and independently reproduced without exposing host assets.

ai-model.title: AI system and model inventory
ai-model.technique: Inventory models, providers, versions, modalities, prompts, retrieval, tools, data, policies, guardrails, hosting, and external dependencies.
ai-model.oracle: Every supplied or observed AI component and trust boundary is versioned, provenance-bound, and either assessed or explicitly unknown.

ai-model.title: Direct and indirect prompt injection
ai-model.technique: Compare trusted and untrusted instruction channels, encodings, retrieval contexts, modalities, and tool-facing content across bounded tasks.
ai-model.oracle: Untrusted content cannot override higher-priority intent, disclose protected context, or authorize an unintended action.

ai-model.title: AI sensitive-data leakage
ai-model.technique: Use consented canaries and access-controlled corpora to test memorization, retrieval, context, output, logging, and cross-user disclosure.
ai-model.oracle: Protected data and canaries are not disclosed outside the declared identity, purpose, source, and output policy.

ai-model.title: Unsafe model output handling
ai-model.technique: Compare model outputs across downstream renderers, parsers, tools, code paths, and policy controls using inert harmful-content substitutes.
ai-model.oracle: Model output is treated as untrusted data and cannot directly create unsafe code, markup, command, or consequential effects.

ai-model.title: Excessive model agency
ai-model.technique: Compare requested intent with available tools, permissions, autonomy, confirmation, reversibility, and observed effects across bounded scenarios.
ai-model.oracle: The model cannot initiate or expand consequential action beyond explicit user intent, authority, confirmation, and budget.

ai-model.title: Model and tool interface abuse
ai-model.technique: Exercise bounded schema, parameter, error, retry, delegation, and composition variants at model and tool boundaries.
ai-model.oracle: Tool use remains schema-valid, purpose-bound, least-authority, observable, and unable to bypass policy through composition.

ai-model.title: AI data, model, and retrieval poisoning
ai-model.technique: Introduce consented labeled perturbations into disposable datasets, artifacts, or retrieval sources and compare influence, provenance, and recovery.
ai-model.oracle: Untrusted or changed data and artifacts cannot silently alter model behavior outside declared provenance and validation controls.

ai-model.title: AI resource and denial-of-service controls
ai-model.technique: Increase approved token, context, media, concurrency, retry, tool, and recursive-work dimensions within explicit cost and time limits.
ai-model.oracle: AI workload cost, latency, memory, recursion, and external effects remain bounded per request, identity, and service policy.

ai-model.title: Model and detector evasion
ai-model.technique: Apply bounded semantic-preserving, encoding, modality, and adversarial perturbations to compare policy and classifier consistency.
ai-model.oracle: Equivalent disallowed intent does not bypass control solely through representation, modality, or bounded perturbation.

ai-model.title: Hallucination, grounding, and claim integrity
ai-model.technique: Use source-controlled answerable, unanswerable, conflicting, stale, and citation tasks to compare evidence attribution and uncertainty.
ai-model.oracle: Material claims remain supported by bound sources or are explicitly reported as uncertain or unsupported.

ai-model.title: AI privacy and inference resistance
ai-model.technique: Use consented membership, attribute, inversion, linkage, retention, and cross-context probes with calibrated statistical controls.
ai-model.oracle: The measured system does not reveal protected membership, attributes, content, or identity beyond the declared privacy budget and access policy.

ai-model.title: AI model supply-chain integrity
ai-model.technique: Bind models, adapters, tokenizers, prompts, datasets, code, runtime, registries, signatures, licenses, and provenance through deployment.
ai-model.oracle: Only approved content-addressed AI artifacts and dependencies reach the runtime, with provenance and policy intact.

agentic.title: Agent trust and consequence inventory
agentic.technique: Inventory agents, models, tools, skills, memory, identities, protocols, handoffs, policies, approvals, trust boundaries, and consequential actions.
agentic.oracle: Every observed agent authority and consequence path is target-bound, provenance-tagged, and either assessed or explicitly unknown.

agentic.title: Agent tool authorization
agentic.technique: Compare tool visibility, schema, identity, purpose, approval, parameter, effect, and revocation behavior across roles and states.
agentic.oracle: A tool call occurs only with current identity, intended purpose, least authority, validated parameters, and required approval.

agentic.title: MCP identity, consent, and capability boundaries
agentic.technique: Inspect discovery, transport, server identity, tool/resource metadata, capability negotiation, consent, invocation, and change detection.
agentic.oracle: MCP authority remains bound to the intended server, client, user, capability, approved invocation, and unchanged metadata.

agentic.title: A2A identity, consent, and task boundaries
agentic.technique: Inspect agent-card provenance, peer identity, task delegation, message integrity, artifacts, callbacks, consent, and authority propagation.
agentic.oracle: A2A messages and tasks are authentic, intended, consented, least-authority, and unable to inherit undeclared upstream authority.

agentic.title: Agent memory and context poisoning
agentic.technique: Use labeled untrusted memories and retrieval items to test write authority, provenance, priority, lifetime, retrieval, correction, and cross-user isolation.
agentic.oracle: Untrusted memory cannot silently become authoritative, persist beyond policy, cross identities, or trigger unintended action.

agentic.title: Agent skill, plugin, and tool supply chain
agentic.technique: Bind metadata, package, implementation, publisher, permissions, signatures, update, approval-time, and runtime identities by digest.
agentic.oracle: Only reviewed content-addressed skills and tools execute, and approval-time identity and behavior match runtime.

agentic.title: Cross-agent trust boundaries
agentic.technique: Compare authenticated and unauthenticated peer messages, provenance, roles, namespaces, content trust, and downstream authority.
agentic.oracle: Peer output is treated as untrusted and cannot cross identity or authority boundaries without validation and explicit delegation.

agentic.title: Agent delegation and authority propagation
agentic.technique: Trace task, identity, scope, budget, expiry, evidence, and revocation through bounded delegation and nested handoff chains.
agentic.oracle: Delegated authority never exceeds the delegator, stated task, scope, budget, validity, or revocation state.

agentic.title: Agent confused-deputy resistance
agentic.technique: Present lower-trust requests through higher-authority agents while varying requester, resource, intent, and delegation evidence.
agentic.oracle: An agent cannot use its authority for a requester or purpose lacking equivalent direct authorization.

agentic.title: Agent goal and instruction manipulation
agentic.technique: Compare direct, indirect, retrieved, delayed, encoded, and cross-agent instructions against explicit operator goals and instruction priority.
agentic.oracle: Lower-trust instructions cannot replace, hide, or redirect the authorized goal or its safety constraints.

agentic.title: Hidden and persistent state transitions
agentic.technique: Compare fresh and stateful runs across memory, caches, files, sessions, tools, scheduled work, and delayed actions using resettable generations.
agentic.oracle: Security-relevant state changes are observable, attributable, bounded in lifetime, and reset or disclosed as declared.

agentic.title: Agent audit and evidence bypass
agentic.technique: Compare declared actions with trace, tool, network, process, memory, approval, and artifact evidence under loss, reordering, and evasion attempts.
agentic.oracle: Consequential actions cannot complete without required independent evidence, and evidence loss or contradiction fails closed.
